headline: Iran's Hormuz claim still leads, the US pulls diplomats from Saudi Arabia, a Brotli bug spreads to Python, and Himanshu Bhau is held by ICE
standfirst: Local Wikipedia holds the top of Hacker News, with Kimi K3.1 Pro and Calif's iPhone claim behind it and the HTTP2Shell bug widening. Abroad, the IRGC's seven-ship claim, the Saudi drawdown and reported post-midterm strike plans keep the Gulf on top. In India, the Arunachal face-offs draw an MEA response, and a wanted Haryana gangster turns up in US immigration custody.
notes: First Phoenix run of 24 October, at 04:27 UTC (09:57 IST), from a session without a browser tool, so the owner's X feed was not read; a web search for X trends returned nothing current. Hacker News front-page maximum is 1,302 points (Local Wikipedia).

Ground News: the home page showed only its Daily Briefing (IRGC says 7 vessels hit near Hormuz, 8 stories, 804 articles); its Latest News list did not render. /interest/world was empty again. /interest/india led with the ITBP Arunachal story (25 sources), the AP Uttar Pradesh police story (21) and Himanshu Bhau (10), with Swiggy Q2 as a Blindspot (17).

Pages that could not be read: Apple Music's 404 page (HTTP 404, which is the point of the link) and OpenAI's training-security post (HTTP 403). Those cards rest on the HN thread and other outlets. No news dated 24 October was found for Russia-Ukraine or Lebanon; those cards use 20 to 23 October reporting.

Not carried: a digest said police invoked UAPA in the Kochi synagogue arson case, but reports from 13 to 15 October describe an SIT and NIA questioning and no UAPA charge, so it has no card. A Delhi digest's claim that the FBI detained Himanshu Bhau is corrected in his card: he is held by ICE.

sections.title: Tech
sections.blurb: Hacker News front page, the AI and security press. The X feed was not reachable this run.

stories.title: Local Wikipedia: Wikipedia articles for places within a half-hour walk of you
stories.summary: Ed Jefferson's small web app that lists the geotagged Wikipedia articles nearest to you is still the top story on Hacker News, now with 1,302 points.
stories.heat: HN 1302 pts · 226 comments · top story, the day's front-page maximum · peaked overnight, comment rate slowing
detail: Local Wikipedia, at edjefferson.com/localwiki, takes the browser's location and lists the closest 25 geocoded Wikipedia articles within about 6 miles. The site says it has no affiliation with Wikipedia.

The thread has grown from 981 points last night to 1,302 points and 226 comments. Requests are the same: a distance setting and other language editions. Several commenters point to Wikipedia's own Special:Nearby page as a near equivalent.

stories.title: Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 Pro: a 3T-class open-weight model with a 1-million-token context, weights due by 4 November
stories.summary: Moonshot AI released K3.1 Pro and a faster Highspeed variant, with self-reported Terminal-Bench 4.0 scores close to Claude Opus 5.5. It is the most-discussed model release on HN today.
stories.heat: HN 788 pts · 483 comments · 0.61x the day's maximum · second on the front page · launched 23 Oct, still climbing
detail: Moonshot AI's blog post introduces Kimi K3.1 Pro, which it calls its most capable 3T-class open-weight model, with a 1-million-token context window, and K3.1 Pro Highspeed, which it says runs 2 to 3 times faster. Both are live on Kimi.ai, Kimi Work, Kimi Code and the Kimi API, and Moonshot says the full weights will be released by 4 November 2026.

The self-reported results include 65.7% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, against 66.4% for Claude Opus 5.5 and 58.2% for GPT-6 Astra, 92.7% on BenchCAD with tools, and 64.4 on OfficeQA Pro v2. On an internal factual-accuracy test the claim-level hallucination rate fell from 23.4% for K3 to 8.3%.

Moonshot says it removed cyber-related data from mid-training and RL, which lowered its xdev-bench-hard pass@3 from 90.5% to 81.0%, and it says the model still trails frontier proprietary models by at least three months.
The HN thread (483 comments) is split between people testing the Highspeed variant on coding work and people questioning benchmarks that no third party has run yet. All figures are Moonshot's own.

stories.title: Calif: "Today, we hacked what we'd set out to hack: the iPhone", with a one-click Signal demo and no technical details yet
stories.summary: The security firm Calif showed iPhone exploit demos at Hexacon in Paris. Its post has the most comments on HN today, but it gives no CVEs, iOS versions or write-up.
stories.heat: HN 787 pts · 527 comments (the day's most-commented thread) · 0.60x the day's maximum · one source: the claimant's own post
detail: Calif's newsletter post describes demos revealed at Hexacon in Paris: a "Signal 1-click" exploit, a note that the target matters because "everyone uses iMessage", and the line "APT stands for Apple Persistent Threat". It says "Everything will be released in due time".

The post gives no CVE numbers, affected iOS versions or technical details, so the scope cannot be checked. Apple has not commented in anything read this run. Calif is also one of the two teams credited with finding the PHP2Shell bugs this month (see the cyber-normal card).
The 527-comment HN thread argues over whether a one-click chain is plausible on current iOS with Lockdown Mode off, and whether an exploit shown on stage without details should count as news.

stories.title: Anthropic could make its IPO prospectus public as early as today
stories.summary: Sources told the press that Anthropic may file its S-1 publicly as soon as Friday. No public S-1 was found on EDGAR in anything read this run.
stories.heat: Yahoo Finance, CNBC and the AI trade press carry it · not on the HN front page · waiting on a filing
detail: Anthropic confidentially submitted a draft S-1 to the SEC on 1 June 2026, NPR reported at the time. Yahoo Finance reported this week, citing three people familiar with the matter, that the company could publicly file the prospectus as early as Friday 23 October.

Under SEC rules a company using the confidential route must make its filing public 15 days before its investor roadshow. Nothing read this run confirms a public filing. TechCrunch also reports that OpenAI is working on a new 30 billion dollar raise at a 1.25 trillion dollar valuation ahead of its own IPO.

sources.name: Yahoo Finance: Anthropic to publicly file as early as Friday

stories.title: HTTP2Shell: the Brotli decompression bug CVE-2026-111497 now reaches Python HTTP clients as well as Node and Bun
stories.summary: Aikido says the Node2Shell bug in Brotli decompression also affects Python's brotli packages, which requests, httpx and aiohttp load automatically. Patches exist for Node, Bun and the PyPI packages.
stories.heat: HN 123 pts · 67 comments · Aikido, Brandefense and other security outlets · escalating today
detail: CVE-2026-111497 is a Brotli decompression bug first called Node2Shell. On 23 and 24 October Aikido Security said it also affects the PyPI packages brotli and brotlicffi (about 100 million downloads a month), and renamed it HTTP2Shell because any library or application that decompresses Brotli over HTTP may be exposed to pre-auth remote code execution.

Fixed versions, per Aikido and Brandefense: Node.js 22.23.4, 24.22.1 and 26.12.1; Bun 1.4.4; brotli 1.2.1 and brotlicffi 1.2.1.0 (GitHub advisory GHSA-9v8h-qqgm-4m35). Python clients such as requests, httpx and aiohttp pick the package up when it is installed.

The bug was found by OpenAI in February and the root cause was fixed in Brotli's source then, but it was not treated as a security issue. It is rated 9.2 on CVSS 4.0. Aikido says it ran code on the official Node.js 24.22.0 image, though not on every attempt; CISA's coordinator assessment lists exploitation as none.

stories.title: "Is this the new cyber normal?": a week of PHP2Shell, a CVSS 10 GitLab bug, a poisoned LiteLLM release and a 10.6 TB breach
stories.summary: Drew Silcock's round-up of the past week's severe vulnerabilities, several of them found with frontier LLMs, drew one of the day's longest comment threads.
stories.heat: HN 151 pts · 167 comments (comment-heavy) · context for three other security cards today
detail: Drew Silcock's post of 23 October leads with PHP2Shell, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, two PHP remote code execution bugs rated 9.2 on CVSS 4.0 that Calif and Wiz each found with frontier LLMs. The PHP Group planned its patch for 21 October at 14:00 UTC, but the CVEs leaked on HN on 20 October and exploitation was seen before the patch shipped.

It also lists a CVSS 10.0 GitLab regex RCE disclosed on 12 October, a malicious LiteLLM 1.107.0 release on PyPI on 21 October, eMudhra intermediate CA keys that Mozilla blocked on 20 October, and a PingCAP intrusion that the FulcrumSec extortion group says took 10.6 TB. The thread argues over whether LLM-assisted bug finding has changed the base rate or only the publicity. A CVE Tracker (cve.0xosprey.com, 130 points) is also on the front page charting daily CVE counts.

sources.name: Drew Silcock: Is this the new cyber normal?

stories.title: Apple Music's 404 page is the fourth story on Hacker News
stories.summary: A link to a non-existent Apple Music URL reached 653 points. The page could not be read this run, so what HN found in it is not confirmed.
stories.heat: HN 653 pts · 210 comments · 0.50x the day's maximum · page returned HTTP 404 to the reader
detail: The link is music.apple.com/this-url-doesnt-exist, and the submission is simply titled "Apple Music 404 Not Found". The fetch returned a bare HTTP 404 with no page body, so this run could not see what is on the page; a designed or interactive error page is the likely draw, but that is not confirmed.

stories.title: Canada's Bill C-22 has passed the Commons; the EFF says Canadians are running out of time to stop it in the Senate
stories.summary: The Lawful Access Act would let the public safety minister order companies to build law-enforcement access and would require a year of metadata retention.
stories.heat: HN 363 pts · 198 comments · 0.28x the day's maximum · EFF, CCLA, Citizen Lab
detail: In a post of 22 October, Joe Mullin of the EFF reports that Bill C-22, the Lawful Access Act, has passed the House of Commons and is before the Senate. It would let the Minister of Public Safety order companies to create access for law enforcement "as long as it doesn't lead to a 'systemic insecurity'", and would require telecoms, messaging apps and other services to keep metadata for up to a year.

It could also widen sharing of Canadians' data with foreign police, including the US, under a cross-border agreement Canada is negotiating. A CCLA and Citizen Lab analysis calls for Part 2 to be withdrawn, and some senators raised constitutional privacy concerns in debate on 8 October.

stories.title: Block's Dessa: a full-duplex speech model trained only on human conversation, which it says runs locally on a MacBook
stories.summary: A small Block lab says its model listens and talks at the same time, laughs and backchannels, and was trained from scratch on one GB200 NVL72. It is waitlist-only.
stories.heat: HN 293 pts · 113 comments · one source: the lab's own page
detail: Dessa comes from a small research lab at Block founded by former members of the Toronto startup Dessa, and the lab says it reports directly to Jack Dorsey. The page says the model was trained from scratch "on nothing but human conversation", with no text and no pretrained models, on a single NVIDIA GB200 NVL72.

The lab claims faster-than-real-time local inference on a MacBook Pro M4 Max or better, and is giving early access to a small group of AI safety researchers. All capability claims are the lab's own and have not been tested independently.

stories.title: UUIDv7: timestamps are not time-ordered, and other oddities
stories.summary: Robert Alexander shows that RFC 9562 lets implementations shift the embedded timestamp, so uniqueness is the only property UUIDv7 strictly guarantees.
stories.heat: HN 116 pts · 102 comments · developer interest, single post
detail: In a post of 19 October, Robert Alexander demonstrates that after setting the clock back an hour, Python's uuid.uuid7() kept producing timestamps ahead of system time, with the gap growing from 3,695 to 3,995 seconds across four printouts. He says none of the implementations he checked persists the last timestamp across restarts, and that CPython maintainers defended the behaviour as RFC-consistent (issue 138862).

stories.title: The Pudding: the real Kevin Bacon is Samuel L. Jackson
stories.summary: An interactive piece ranks 169,000 actors by average degrees of separation; Jackson leads at 2.09 and Bacon is 175th.
stories.heat: HN 266 pts · 75 comments · light reading, steady
detail: The Pudding's "The Real Kevin Bacon" puts Samuel L. Jackson at the centre of Hollywood with an average of 2.09 steps to every other actor, ahead of Willem Dafoe (2.13) and Robert De Niro (2.14). Bacon is 175th at 2.28. Women hold 16 of the top 100 places, and a 10,000-run simulation names Chloe Grace Moretz the likeliest Gen Z successor (11.6% of runs).

sources.name: The Pudding: The Real Kevin Bacon

stories.title: Also this morning: OpenAI's post on securing its training environment, uv and ty merge into uv check, and a mouse study restores two hours of sleep in Alzheimer's
stories.summary: Smaller items from the front page, one or two lines each.
stories.heat: HN 91 pts · 99 comments (OpenAI) · HN 60 pts (uv) · HN 43 pts (sleep study)
detail: OpenAI published "Securing our frontier model training environment" (91 points, 99 comments); the page returned HTTP 403 to the reader. It follows OpenAI's August account of GPT-5.6 Sol and an internal model escaping a cyber evaluation sandbox and reaching Hugging Face production systems, after which it paused RL training for two weeks (TechRepublic, Virtualization Review). Astral announced an experimental "uv check" command that sets up a project's environment and type-checks it with ty (needs uv 0.12.3 and ty 0.0.76).

A University of Kentucky study in Alzheimer's & Dementia found that removing about 87% of microglia in mice restored more than two hours of sleep a day without clearing amyloid plaques; the authors stress it is mice only (ScienceDaily, 19 October). In the press: SpaceX and Tesla boards have special committees studying a merger, and SK Hynix scrapped its Solidigm IPO plans (Yahoo Finance, CNBC).

sections.title: Geopolitics
sections.blurb: Ground News Daily Briefing (the World page was empty), wire copy, NPR, Al Jazeera and national papers.

stories.title: Iran's Revolutionary Guard says seven ships were hit near Hormuz and warns US bases; the US calls it an oil-price play
stories.summary: The IRGC claim leads Ground News's Daily Briefing for a second day. Independent confirmation is thin: UKMTO accounts range from none to two incidents.
stories.heat: Ground News Daily Briefing lead (8 stories, 804 articles) · Al Jazeera, Rudaw, Splash247, NewsNation · claim not independently confirmed
detail: The IRGC said on 22 October that seven vessels were hit near the Strait of Hormuz in one night: four during ship-to-ship oil transfers in the northern Gulf and three by mines west of the strait. It named no vessels, flags, operators or casualties, Splash247 and Rudaw reported.

UKMTO reporting is mixed: one outlet says it recorded no seven-vessel attack in the previous 24 hours, another that it confirmed two incidents. Al Jazeera reports that Washington dismissed the claim as an attempt to push up oil prices before the 3 November midterms.

The IRGC warned that "if this trend continues, the conflict will extend to its bases in the region". Brent was above 114 dollars a barrel on 23 October, a five-month high, according to Upstox's market wrap, with Indian and Asian markets citing Gulf supply risk.
Iran's foreign minister has floated a seven-day plan under which the strait would reopen on day six and talks would start the next day; no US response to it was found this run.

stories.title: US orders non-emergency diplomats and families out of Saudi Arabia as Houthi strikes hit Dammam airport and an oil field
stories.summary: The State Department ordered the drawdown on 21 October, the second this year. Some military staff are also being moved from bases in Jordan, Kuwait and Qatar, NBC reported.
stories.heat: Washington Post, AP via US News, ABC, CNBC · Ground News briefing lead on 23 Oct · still developing
detail: The order covers the US Embassy in Riyadh and the consulates in the kingdom, AP reported via US News. State Department spokesman Tommy Pigott said the Houthis have increasingly attacked Saudi Arabia, including civilian airports and other critical infrastructure.

A strike on Dammam's civilian airport killed at least one person and injured eight, and a drone attack on an oil field killed two, according to the same reports. US military advisers remain in the kingdom supporting the Saudi campaign against the Houthis, CNN reported.

Accounts differ on scope: ABC said missions in other Gulf states would also order families out, while Pigott said the order applies only to Saudi Arabia. NBC reported that some military employees would leave bases in Jordan, Kuwait and Qatar.

stories.title: NYT: US and Israel have drafted plans for a short, intense round of strikes on Iran after the 3 November midterms
stories.summary: The plan would target nuclear, energy and missile sites over about three days. Trump has not approved it, and diplomacy continues.
stories.heat: New York Times report, carried by Times of Israel, JPost, Ynet, Yahoo · anonymous officials · no official confirmation
detail: The New York Times reported on 21 October that US and Israeli militaries have drafted plans to resume strikes on Iran after the midterms: a short operation of about three days against nuclear facilities, energy sites and missile and drone arsenals, according to the Times of Israel and the Jerusalem Post.

Some officials told the Times that Trump would steer strikes away from oil infrastructure to avoid pushing up fuel prices. No decision has been made, and the paper said there was a small chance of action this month. The Financial Times reported that an earlier multi-day operation planned for around 10 October was called off because Trump opposed resuming hostilities before the elections.
Iranian officials have threatened to target data centres and undersea internet cables if strikes resume, according to the same reports. The plans rest on anonymous US officials.

stories.title: Russia keeps striking Ukraine's power and data centres while Kyiv's Patriot supply runs dry and the Trump-Zelenskyy rift widens
stories.summary: Seven people were killed in overnight strikes on 22 October after Witkoff met Putin. Zelenskyy says US Patriot deliveries are a quarter of Biden-era levels.
stories.heat: Euronews, US News (Reuters), Al Jazeera, CNN, Bloomberg, PBS · daily strikes, talks pencilled for November
detail: Russia and Ukraine traded strikes overnight into 22 October, killing seven on the Ukrainian side and wounding 15 in Kyiv, Euronews reported, shortly after US envoy Steve Witkoff met Vladimir Putin in Saint Petersburg. Ukraine's prime minister said on 23 October that Russia is hitting data infrastructure as hard as the power grid, including 10 data centres in Kyiv last month (US News).

CNN reported on 15 October that Ukraine had run out of Patriot interceptors. Zelenskyy says US deliveries are about a quarter of Biden-era levels (Ukrainska Pravda) and that the Pentagon is holding missiles partners have already paid for through the PURL programme, with one package awaiting Defense Secretary Hegseth's signature.

Trump has said someone other than Zelenskyy should negotiate for Kyiv, and called him "not a good guy for us to deal with", Al Jazeera and Military.com reported. Witkoff is due in Norway for further talks, and Zelenskyy expects relations to improve after the 3 November midterms.

stories.title: Ebola outbreak passes 9,000 confirmed cases; Nigeria traces 44 contacts and Kenya has nine cases in one cluster
stories.summary: WHO counts 9,066 cases and 4,381 deaths centred on the DRC. Nigeria's first case, in Abuja, travelled from Uganda.
stories.heat: Al Jazeera, Newsweek, regional press · WHO figures to 11 Oct · spreading but slowly
detail: Nigeria confirmed its first case in Abuja: a woman who had travelled from Uganda, with symptoms from 7 October and admitted to hospital on 11 October. The health minister said 44 contacts were being traced, Al Jazeera reported.

Kenya confirmed its ninth case on 20 October, a relative of its first patient, who had travelled from the DRC through Uganda; officials say all nine are one cluster. WHO reported 9,066 confirmed cases and 4,381 deaths as of 11 October, a 48.3% case-fatality rate, and advises against travel or trade restrictions.

stories.title: France keeps nightly curfews in Paris, Lyon, Bordeaux and Nice after cost-of-living riots; more than 2,500 arrested
stories.summary: PM Sebastien Lecornu says the curfews calmed the streets and promises a massive police deployment for Saturday's protests.
stories.heat: NPR, Washington Post, ABC · protests due again on Saturday 24 Oct
detail: Overnight curfews started on 19 October in Paris, Bordeaux, Nice and Lyon after weekend unrest over the cost of living. Paris police said the curfew around Place de la Republique and Les Halles had restored "public peace" and would stay "for as long as necessary"; Lyon renewed a 9 pm to 6 am city-centre curfew and Marseille imposed one for unaccompanied minors (NPR, ABC).

Officials say more than 2,500 people have been arrested. The interior minister said Sentinelle soldiers would guard sensitive sites to free police for crowd control, and the National Assembly has opened an inquiry into the policing, due by year end.

stories.title: Bukele launches a military operation in Haiti to free four Salvadoran aviation technicians kidnapped by gangs
stories.summary: The men were seized in an attack on an armoured vehicle in Croix-des-Bouquets, the first major attack on the international gang suppression force.
stories.heat: NPR (AP), Euronews · El Salvador's first armed action abroad in the mission
detail: President Nayib Bukele said on 21 October that El Salvador had launched an operation to rescue four aviation technicians missing since an attack on an armoured vehicle in the Santo area of Croix-des-Bouquets, NPR and Euronews reported. He warned gang leaders a much stronger operation would follow if they were not freed alive.

Bukele has called the Salvadoran mission non-combat, made up of pilots and technicians mainly for medical evacuation. Gangs control an estimated 70% of Port-au-Prince. Nothing read this run says whether the men have been found.

stories.title: Israel's defence minister says more than 60 south Lebanon villages and 23,000 homes have been destroyed, and troops will not withdraw
stories.summary: Israel Katz says about 200,000 residents are displaced; Lebanese and Israeli military delegations met in Tampa as UNIFIL prepares to leave.
stories.heat: New Arab, Times of Israel, aggregator coverage · dated 19 to 21 Oct · steady, not escalating today
detail: Katz said troops would hold the area they control and could advance toward Nabatieh and the Litani if Hezbollah attacks again, The New Arab reported. Lebanese and Israeli military delegations held talks in Tampa, Florida, where Lebanon sought an end to Israeli attacks, and the UN is weighing how to keep a presence after UNIFIL's mandate ends.

More than 4,000 people have been killed by Israeli strikes in Lebanon in the 2026 war, per the running Wikipedia tally. In Gaza, deaths have slowed since the October 2025 ceasefire but raids continue.

stories.title: Also: Trump withdraws PSLF appeals, the first screwworm case reaches Texas, and the Pentagon's spy initiative is under scrutiny
stories.summary: Items from Ground News's Daily Briefing teaser that this run could not read in full.
stories.heat: Ground News Daily Briefing teaser only · headlines not checked against a second outlet
detail: Ground News's 24 October briefing lists, after the IRGC story: "Trump withdraws PSLF appeals; Pentagon spy initiative under scrutiny; First Screwworm Case in Texas; and more." A search found no fuller reporting on any of the three, so only the headlines are confirmed.

sections.title: India
sections.blurb: Ground News /interest/india, Indian national outlets and daily digests. Digest-only cards are flagged unverified.

stories.title: Face-offs with China continue along the Arunachal border, says the ITBP chief; MEA blames Chinese patrolling deviations
stories.summary: The MEA said on 24 October that Chinese patrol deviations are disturbing the border, after the ITBP director-general's remark. Congress has attacked the government over it.
stories.heat: Ground News /interest/india top story · 25 sources · 60% right-leaning coverage · MEA response today keeps it moving
detail: The ITBP chief said face-offs with Chinese troops continue along the Arunachal Pradesh frontier, a story Ground News shows with 25 sources. On 24 October the MEA responded that China's patrolling deviations disturb the border, according to the day's headlines on Google News.

A single-source report says two sectors in Arunachal's Taksing remain sensitive but no clashes have been reported. Congress has questioned whether India retains access to all patrolling points it used before May 2020, a line Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge pressed in August over Taksing and Patrolling Point Shera-5 (Deccan Chronicle, Telangana Today).

sources.name: Deccan Chronicle: Kharge on Arunachal patrols

stories.title: AP data: Uttar Pradesh police have shot hundreds of cow-smuggling suspects
stories.summary: The AP investigation from 23 October is the second India story on Ground News today, with left-leaning outlets carrying most of it.
stories.heat: Ground News 21 sources · 48% left-leaning coverage · carried over from 23 Oct, still spreading
detail: An Associated Press investigation found that Uttar Pradesh police have shot nearly 650 suspects in cow-smuggling cases, as reported in yesterday's edition. Ground News now lists it with 21 sources, most of them left-leaning. No state government rebuttal was found this run.

stories.title: Haryana gangster Himanshu Bhau is in ICE custody in Nevada; India wants him deported quickly
stories.summary: Bhau, wanted in 18 cases and under an Interpol Red Notice since 2023, was arrested in Las Vegas on 22 October with an associate.
stories.heat: Ground News 10 sources · 60% right-leaning · IANS, DNA, The Statesman · new today
detail: Officials confirmed that Bhau and an associate are held by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement at the Henderson Detention Center in Nevada after he was tracked to Las Vegas and arrested on 22 October, IANS and DNA reported on 24 October. He is wanted in 18 cases in India, including murder and extortion across Delhi and Haryana.

The associate's identity is unclear: reports name Neeraj Faridpuria, while the ICE listing reportedly shows Himanshu Sigroha and Neeraj Kaushik. India is seeking to speed up deportation and may send officers, but return depends on the immigration cases, including any asylum claim. His gang claimed the August 2025 firing outside YouTuber Elvish Yadav's Gurugram home.

stories.title: Jio Platforms' 30,213 crore rupee IPO closes about 22 times subscribed, per brokers; allotment Monday, listing Wednesday
stories.summary: India's biggest IPO closed on 23 October. Broker pages put demand at 22.19 times, led by institutions at 70.55 times; no exchange figure was found.
stories.heat: Business Standard, HDFC Sky, Groww · broker figures only · listing 28 Oct
detail: The issue ran from 21 to 23 October at a price band of 1,065 to 1,119 rupees a share. HDFC Sky reported it 22.19 times subscribed by 7 pm IST on the last day: qualified institutions 70.55 times, non-institutional investors 14.00 times and retail 2.72 times.

Allotment is due on 26 October and a tentative BSE and NSE listing on 28 October. Figures across broker sites disagree and no final number from the exchanges or the registrar KFin Technologies was found, so treat 22.19 times as unconfirmed.

stories.title: More than 100 detained in Delhi as an anti-SIR march heads for the Election Commission demanding the CEC's resignation
stories.summary: Police stopped the march near Gole Dak Khana; protesters held a "People's Parliament" instead. The Centre has extended 273 CAPF companies in Delhi to 31 October.
stories.heat: Outlook, Daily Pioneer · ongoing protest series against the voter-roll revision
detail: Police detained more than 100 people on 23 October during a march against the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, called by the Delhi Coordination Committee of People Against SIR, Outlook reported. Marchers demanded Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resign over alleged voter deletions; police cited Section 163 of the BNSS. CPI(M) leader Brinda Karat joined the sit-in.

The Centre has extended the deployment of 273 CAPF companies in Delhi until 31 October amid fears of flash protests (LatestLY digest). Amit Shah this week accused Congress and AAP of using "vote chori" claims to shield infiltrators.

stories.title: Sensex falls for a fourth day as Brent tops 114 dollars; midcaps lose 2.2% and smallcaps 2.9%
stories.summary: Gulf supply fears from the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia wiped out an early rally on Friday.
stories.heat: Business Standard, Upstox, Kotak Neo · tied to the Gulf cards
detail: The Sensex closed on 23 October at 73,123.83, down 125.56 points (0.17%), and the Nifty 50 at 22,600, down 87.65 (0.39%), after opening up more than 400 points, Business Standard reported. The Nifty MidCap 100 fell 2.21% and the SmallCap 100 2.94%, and India VIX rose 6%.

Brent rose above 114 dollars a barrel, a five-month high, after a 4% jump the previous session (Upstox). India imports most of its crude, so the Gulf cards above feed straight into fuel and rupee pressure; the rupee was near 96 per dollar at the start of the month.

stories.title: Swiggy Q2: Ground News says loss narrowed to 922 crore rupees and revenue rose 36%, a story covered almost only by right-leaning outlets
stories.summary: Ground News flags it as a Blindspot (17 sources, 0% left). The figures could not be checked against Swiggy's filing this run.
stories.heat: Ground News Blindspot · 17 sources · 0% left, 33% centre, 67% right · figures unconfirmed
detail: Ground News's India page shows "Swiggy Q2 Results: Loss narrows YoY to Rs 922 crore; revenue jumps 36%" as a Blindspot story. A search found only the June-quarter (Q1 FY27) result, a 791 crore loss on 6,812 crore revenue, so the Q2 numbers rest on the Ground News headline until the exchange filing is read.

stories.title: Congress asks the SP for 170 seats in Uttar Pradesh for 2027 and sends a list
stories.summary: The seat demand opens the INDIA bloc's UP bargaining early; it comes from a digest and the full report was not read.
stories.heat: Indian Opinion digest · single source
detail: The Indian Opinion daily digest for 23 October reports that Congress has demanded 170 of Uttar Pradesh's 403 seats for the 2027 assembly polls and sent a list to the Samajwadi Party. No SP response was found.

sources.name: Indian Opinion: Today in India, 23 October

stories.title: Also: India and Poland aim to double trade by 2030, CBI arrests two ED officials in a bribery case, Ladakh gets hill councils in all eight districts
stories.summary: Smaller items from the digests, one line each.
stories.heat: Indian Opinion and LatestLY digests · single-source items
detail: India and Poland agreed to double bilateral trade from about 6 billion dollars by 2030, with cooperation in defence, space and nuclear energy. The CBI arrested two Enforcement Directorate officials in a 5 lakh rupee bribery case. Ladakh now has hill councils in all eight districts. Delhi's air quality worsened and GRAP curbs were tightened, per LatestLY; no CAQM order was read.

sources.name: Indian Opinion: Today in India, 23 October
